anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same system GND net.
anomalies.expected: For the intended isolated CAN buses, GND1 and GND2 of each isolated CAN transceiver should be separate ground domains, not tied together.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: This defeats the galvanic isolation of the CAN interfaces and can introduce ground loops or noise coupling between the logic side and the CAN side.

anomalies.observed: The second LED element of D30 has its anode pin D30.4 connected directly to ESTOP_OUT, while its cathode pin D30.2 is connected through R60 to the same ESTOP_OUT net.
anomalies.expected: An indicator LED should have its anode tied to a supply or LED-power net and its cathode driven by the status signal through a current-limit resistor, as done for D30.3/D30.1 and the other LEDs on /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The second element of D30 cannot light because both terminals are held at the same potential, so the intended ESTOP indicator function is lost.

parsed.summary: The build contains at least two deviations: the isolated CAN transceiver grounds are shorted to common GND, defeating the intended CAN isolation, and one LED element of D30 is effectively shorted across itself on ESTOP_OUT.
